data.Charge 1: DISORDERLY CONDUCT - BRAWLING OR FIGHTING; CONTROLLED SUBSTANCE/NARCOTICS

data.Description: The Carver man was found guilty of 16 counts of federal animal crushing charges.
data.Story:
A Carver man is facing a potentially long prison sentence after being found guilty of running a pay-per-view YouTube channel that featured small animals being tortured.

Bryan Wesley Edison, 33, of Carver, was found guilty by a federal jury on 16 counts of animal crushing, which criminalizes the purposeful crushing, burning, drowning, suffocating, impaling, or otherwise subjecting to serious bodily injury to living mammals, birds, reptiles, or amphibians.

According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office of Minnesota, Edison filmed himself deliberately causing serious injury to animals and then posting them to the internet between July 2022 and October 2023.

He ran a series of YouTube channels where he offered a few videos that were free to view, with paid access for other channels ranging from $0.99 to $99.99, and made in excess of $1,500.

“In the videos, the smaller live animals would suffer prolonged torture and death through drowning, crushing, and being dismembered alive by the larger reptiles,” the attorney’s office said.

He would place small, live animals in a space for a “large, exotic reptile” to attack and sometimes eat, and titles for the videos included “Snapping Turtle Gives Rat a Slow Death,” “Dog mauls guinea pig on membership page, while others used words such as “shred,” “screaming,” and “kills mouse brutally” in the descriptions.

Edison could also be heard in the videos providing commentary, including phrases like “this bunny is fighting, maybe it’s too big for Shredder” and “Shredder, do your worst.”

YouTube ultimately removed each of Edison’s channels for violating its policy on violence.

“The defendant tried to make a profit and took pleasure in torturing defenseless animals. His actions were inhumane and illegal, and with this guilty verdict, my office is delivering justice,” said United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen.

“The crimes committed by Bryan Edison were the documentation of cruelty for cruelty’s sake, made more shocking to society by the fact that he sought to profit from that cruelty,” said FBI Minneapolis Field Office Special Agent in Charge Christopher D. Dotson.

“The result of predatory, violent videos like those produced by this defendant is not only needless pain and suffering of the animals being tortured, but serious psychological harm to those who consume the content.”

Edison faces a prison sentence of up to 7 years for each count, plus a $250,000 fine.
